policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'a river of water of life, bright as crystal' with nothing answering RP's added καθαρόν.
ἀποδιδοῦν and ἀποδιδούς differ only in the gender of the participle, and ASV 'yielding its fruit every month' shows no agreement.
ASV reads 'there shall be night no more', and 'no more' renders ἔτι rather than RP's locative ἐκεῖ, which it renders 'there' at 21:25.
οὐκ ἔχουσιν χρείαν and χρείαν οὐκ ἔχουσιν differ only in order, and ASV 'they need no light of lamp' fixes that order by its own syntax.
ASV reads 'they need no light of lamp', whose 'light' answers φωτός; RP's omission would leave only 'no need of a lamp'.
φῶς and φωτός are nominative and genitive of the same noun in the coordinate phrase, and ASV 'neither light of sun' is identical under either.
ASV renders φωτίσει ἐπ᾽ αὐτούς as 'shall give them light' with no separate word for ἐπί, so its presence or absence leaves the English unchanged.
ASV's past tense 'And he said unto me' reflects the aorist εἶπεν, while it renders the present λέγει as 'And he saith unto me' in verses 9, 10, and 17 of this chapter.
The variant is only the article before κύριος, and ASV writes 'the Lord' as it does for that title throughout, whether or not ὁ stands.
ῥυπαρευθήτω and ῥυπανθήτω are alternative aorist passive imperatives of the same sense, both rendered 'let him be made filthy'.
ASV's present 'my reward is with me' reflects ἐστίν rather than the future ἔσται, which it would render 'shall be'.
The variant is only the article before ἀρχή, and ASV writes 'the beginning' under either reading, as it does at 21:6.
The variant is only the article before τέλος, and ASV writes 'the end' under either reading, as it does at 21:6.
ASV reads 'they that wash their robes', which answers πλύνοντες τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν and not RP's ποιοῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, 'that do his commandments'.
ASV's 'God shall add unto him' is a future statement, reflecting the indicative ἐπιθήσει rather than RP's optative ἐπιθήσαι.
ASV's 'God shall take away his part' is a future statement, reflecting the indicative ἀφελεῖ rather than RP's optative ἀφέλοι.
ASV reads 'Yea: I come quickly. Amen: come, Lord Jesus' with a single 'Yea', so its text had no second Ναί before ἔρχου.
ASV reads 'the grace of the Lord Jesus' and footnotes 'Some ancient authorities add Christ', an explicit mapped note keeping Χριστοῦ out of the text.

ASV reads 'be with the saints. Amen.' and footnotes 'Two ancient authorities read with all', which puts πάντων in the margin and τῶν ἁγίων in the text; its closing 'Amen' requires the ἀμήν that only this reading carries.
